items.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024
items.q: I think it was Schoenberg talking about Brahms, about constant variation.

ctx.x: Do you consider your — I’ll just use the word “classical” or “orchestral.” Is it — what’s the term, “through” composed? Which I believe means not necessarily themes developed and returned to.

Yes. There might be a little bit of that — themes — well definitely themes developed. But if I return to something I try not to ever return to it verbatim. There’s a phrase used when people — I think it was Schoenberg talking about Brahms, about constant variation. So you’re really thinking about kind of planting a seed and it growing and never changing. It always turns into something different but you can backtrack and see how it relates to the first little seed that was planted. The Ninth Symphony of Mahler,…

Nice description. I think you just used the term “breaking with tonality.” I hope I’m quoting you correctly. And it makes me think about — I was looking at some of your transcribed solos on line. First of all have you looked at your transcribed solos on line?
